verdict.rationale: Pulumi documents official SDKs in TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, .NET, Java, YAML, and HCL, each covering the full Registry provider surface, plus the Automation API for using the engine itself as an SDK and an ESC SDK. Community users independently report building with the Python SDK and the Automation API. Missing for 10: detailed SDK API-reference or versioning documentation in the evidence, and stronger docs for the Python client (a community user asked for better docs).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: Pulumi supports TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, .NET, Java, YAML, and HCL. Each language is equally capable and supports the full surface area of all Pulumi Registry providers.
Automation API lets you use the Pulumi engine as an SDK, enabling you to create software that can create, update, configure, and destroy infrastructure dynamically.
Use the Pulumi CLI and ESC SDK to manage secrets for a basic OpenAI-based ChatGPT clone.
It worked really well when I used it with Python.
